committed: Before tools/instruments/*.json, the generator, the validator, the adapters or any test existed. Stated plainly: before this file was written the author had read the cited sources once through a summarising fetch (2026-10-28) and had done, by hand and in his head, four things that bear on the bounds below: the plate-scale relation for the five imagers (agreement 0.2 to 1.3 percent), the field against array times pixel scale (agreement 0.3 to 8 percent, the 1.2 degree side of the 0.35 m camera being the worst), the Rubin 5-sigma depth formula against the tabulated depths (a constant offset of about -0.12 to -0.15 mag in all six bands) and the GBT beam in units of lambda over D (about 1.25). The bounds o2.field (10 percent) and o4.rubin-m5 (0.2 mag) were set with those numbers in view and are flagged as such; the others were not. A value that disagrees with its source is a defect in the table, not a tolerance to widen. No value in the table is an estimate: a quantity the source does not state is absent.
rule: Prompt 209, EXECUTION CONTRACT and the validation contract (section 7.5, rule 8): a table of cited facts, not a model. Rule 8(c) (ensembles), (d) (misspecified cases for a method) and (e) (authentic data) do not apply to a table; rule 8(a) and (b) are the structural and cross-check rows below, and 8(d) is the refusal rows (r1 to r8) that the validator must hold.
units: lengths in m (or the unit the source states, converted never), angles in arcsec/arcmin/deg as published, electrons and ADU counts as published, magnitudes as published. A value is stored in the unit the source uses.

s1.facilities.claim: the table holds at least five real facilities, one per class: campus, metre, space, survey, radio

s2.typical.claim: every generic entry has typical: true, is listed apart from the real facilities, and cites the Gravitas teaching default as its source (kind 'typical'); no real facility has typical: true

s3.units.claim: every numeric value carries a unit that parses in js/units/registry.js (a registry id, or registry ids joined by '/') and whose dimension is the parameter's declared dimension

s4.citations.claim: every value names a source in the sources table; every source has a title, a reference or URL (https), a retrieval date (ISO) and a recorded rights basis

s5.absent.claim: a missing value is absent: no null, no NaN, no empty string, no zero standing for unknown

s6.generated.claim: js/data/instruments.js is exactly what tools/build-instruments.mjs writes from tools/instruments/*.json (a prettier fixed point); --check is empty

oracle.note: Independent cross-checks computed from other cited values, never from the value they check. Each applies only where every quantity it needs is present; a check that does not apply is reported N/A with the missing field, never passed.

o1.plate-scale.claim: pixelScale equals 206265 arcsec x pixelSize / focalLength, with focalLength = focalRatio x aperture (the geometric primary)

o2.field.claim: each stated field dimension equals pixels x pixelScale (the gaps between detectors of a mosaic make the product an upper limit for a mosaic's area)

bound.flag: set with the 8 percent disagreement of the 0.35 m camera's short side in view

o3.radio-area.claim: collectingArea equals pi (D/2)^2 for the stated diameter

o3b.radio-beam.claim: the stated half-power beamwidth lies between 1.0 and 1.4 lambda/D at the stated frequency (a tapered dish)

o4.rubin-m5.claim: the tabulated 5-sigma depth in each band equals C_m + 0.50 (m_sky - 21) + 2.5 log10(0.7 / theta_eff) for the same band's tabulated C_m, m_sky and effective seeing (airmass 1, 30 s visit), within the paper's own fudge terms

bound.flag: set with the constant offset of about -0.13 mag in view

o5.zero-point-throughput.claim: a published photometric zero point (magnitude zero point per e-/s) implies a system throughput between 0.10 and 1.00 when compared with an ideal AB photon rate through the same band, computed by the radiation kernel's photonRate() for the collecting area of aperture and obstruction
o5.zero-point-throughput.note: the Las Cumbres paper words its zero points as 'log(e-/s)'; this check is what tells a magnitude zero point from a logarithm, and a leg that fails is a finding about the reading, recorded and not widened

o6.gain-full-well.claim: where gain, full well in electrons and a 16-bit converter are all stated, fullWell / gain does not exceed 65535 counts by more than the stated rounding (10 percent)

refusals.r1: a value with no source is refused
refusals.r2: a value whose source is not in the sources table is refused
refusals.r3: a unit not in the registry is refused
refusals.r4: a unit of the wrong dimension for its parameter is refused
refusals.r5: a null, NaN or non-finite value is refused
refusals.r6: a facility id that a built-in already uses is refused for a pack
refusals.r7: a pack entry that sets typical: true without the teaching-default source is refused
refusals.r8: an unknown parameter name is refused (no silent extra fields)

completeness.reported: per facility and per block, the fields present out of the fields the class expects (the validator's EXPECTED table); reported in INSTRUMENTS.md and the PR, not gated

adopters.a1.planner: the observing-window planner (js/observingWindow.js observingNight) run with a site read from the table agrees with the same call given the site's published numbers by hand, to the last bit
adopters.a2.detector: a detector spec built from a facility reproduces, field by field, the table's gain, readNoise, fullWell and (where present) darkCurrent, lists every field it could not fill, and never fills one
adopters.a3.forward: the ccd forward model run with a setup built from a facility records the table's pixel scale and array in its truth manifest and refuses to run when the table lacks a field the model needs
